name: Message
description: Shows one chat message, styled by who sent it.

role.description: Message role determines styling and alignment

when: Individual turns in a chat transcript
User and assistant turns that must read differently
Turns carrying copy, regenerate, or feedback actions
whenNot: Plain text with no chat context (use Text)
Threads with nested replies (use Card with a custom layout)
guidelines: Always set role — it drives alignment, avatar, and chrome
status covers sending, streaming, and error
Hide avatars with avatar={null}, or showAvatars={false} on ConversationList
User bubbles cap at 80% of the inline measure so the two sides stay distinct
Chrome stays on neutral surfaces; reserve accent for actions and semantic state
Add timestamps once a conversation runs long
Give assistant turns hover actions such as copy and regenerate
accessibility: Uses semantic HTML for message structure
Role-based styling has sufficient color contrast
Streaming indicator respects reduced motion preferences

examples.name: User Message
examples.description: Right-aligned and capped at 80% of the available width.
examples.code:
<Message role="user">
  <Message.Content>
    Hello! Can you help me with a coding question?
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

examples.name: Assistant Message
examples.description: Left-aligned with an avatar and a wider measure.
examples.code:
<Message role="assistant">
  <Message.Content>
    Of course! I'd be happy to help. What would you like to know?
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

examples.name: System Message
examples.description: Centred and quiet, for context rather than conversation.

examples.name: Streaming
examples.description: A blinking caret trails the text as it arrives.
examples.code:
<Message role="assistant" status="streaming">
  <Message.Content>
    I'm currently generating a response for you
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

examples.name: With Timestamp
examples.description: A relative send time sits beneath the bubble.
examples.code:
<Message role="assistant" timestamp={new Date(Date.now() - 300000)}>
  <Message.Content>
    This message was sent 5 minutes ago.
  </Message.Content>
  <Message.Timestamp />
</Message>

examples.name: Error State
examples.description: A failed send turns the bubble and its border red.
examples.code:
<Message role="user" status="error">
  <Message.Content>
    This message failed to send.
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

examples.name: Custom Avatars
examples.description: Photos replace the default glyphs on both sides.
examples.code:
<>
  <Message
    role="user"
    avatar={<Message.Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/64?u=user" alt="Jane" />}
  >
    <Message.Content>
      Can you help me understand this error?
    </Message.Content>
  </Message>
  <Message
    role="assistant"
    avatar={<Message.Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/64?u=bot" alt="AI Assistant" />}
  >
    <Message.Content>
      Sure! Let me take a look at that for you.
    </Message.Content>
  </Message>
</>

examples.name: With Actions
examples.description: Controls stay hidden until the pointer enters the row.
examples.code:
<Message
  role="assistant"
  actions={
    <>
      <Button variant="ghost" size="xs">
        Copy
      </Button>
      <Button variant="ghost" size="xs">
        Regenerate
      </Button>
    </>
  }
>
  <Message.Content>
    Hover over this message to see the actions.
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

relations.note: Messages are typically used within ConversationList
Use Avatar component for custom avatar content
Show ThinkingIndicator while awaiting assistant response

propsSummary: timestamp: Date - when message was sent
avatar: ReactNode - custom avatar (null to hide)
Avatar.src: string - image URL for avatar
Avatar.alt: string - alt text for image avatar
